headline: Highest risk is medium: Notion AI can expose workspace content into a separate document-processing pipeline, but Pathway has no documented write or network surface here.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can ingest workspace pages and team knowledge base content, so malicious instructions embedded there could influence downstream handling. Pathway is a document-processing system with no documented interactive parser or shared channel, so the pairwise injection path is indirect and likely requires manual or workflow bridging.
conditions: IF Notion AI output is copied into Pathway as processing input, injected instructions can propagate.
IF a shared workspace or manual handoff is added between the agents, prompt content becomes attacker-controlled.
mitigations: Strip instructions from Notion-derived text before handing it to Pathway.
Use a fixed template that separates data fields from free text.
Require human review of any Notion-generated summary before ingestion.
Add a provenance tag to all transferred content.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Pathway is a document-processing agent with no declared file or network surfaces. The pair can still leak sensitive workspace data if Notion content is exported into Pathway workflows; uncertainty about Pathway's handling pushes this above low because the data class is sensitive and the bridge is plausible.
conditions: IF workspace pages containing sensitive content are exported from Notion into Pathway, leakage risk exists.
IF Pathway is configured to persist or transform imported documents, copied data may be retained outside Notion.
mitigations: Limit exports to redacted subsets of workspace content.
Review which Notion pages are eligible for transfer.
Disable any automatic document mirroring into Pathway.
Use separate accounts or workspaces for sensitive material.
requires-engineering: add field-level data-loss prevention at the transfer point.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification capability, and Pathway likewise has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification capability. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource documented, there is no plausible capability conflict in this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk changes.
IF an external orchestrator adds shared mutable state, the current none assessment no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared artifacts.
Avoid mounting a common writable directory.
Do not grant git write permissions to either agent.
Monitor for future scope changes in the integration.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI produces workspace-grounded summaries and Q&A, and Pathway is a document-processing pipeline that could consume those outputs as input. If Pathway treats Notion-generated text as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream documents or analytics; the interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Pathway ingests Notion AI summaries without validation, errors can propagate.
IF downstream workflows act on Pathway outputs automatically, the cascade extends beyond a single document.
mitigations: Require source citations on Notion-generated content.
Add a verification step before Pathway ingestion.
Flag low-confidence or uncited statements for review.
Restrict automatic actions based on Pathway outputs.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware validation between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI clearly processes workspace pages and team knowledge base content under vendor-hosted service terms, while Pathway's residency, retention, and certification posture is not documented here. Because the compliance mismatch is not evidenced and Pathway touches no declared sensitive classes, the risk is limited but not zero.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Notion and then exported to Pathway, compliance review is required.
IF Pathway is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules than Notion's vendor hosting, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Classify data before moving it between agents.
Keep regulated records out of the pair unless approved.
Document retention and deletion expectations for both systems.
Review vendor terms for residency and subprocessors.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data flows.
